subclassFeature.name: Path of the Lightning Vessel
entries: A Lightning Vessel is a brute, a monster of battle. Their bodies overflowing with lightning, they arrive unexpectedly, often dropping from buildings or leaping impossible distances, before crashing down amidst the fight. The presence of a single Lightning Vessel is often enough to turn the tides of battle. Their ferocious electricity rampages through their enemies, leaving a trail of charred corpses in their wake. If one ends up face to face against such a monster, there is no running away—they will catch you, electrocute you, and rend your corpse. Although vital in the fight against the Scourge, their recklessness causes fear in the heart of friends and foes alike.

The Scions created the Lightning Vessels, using galvanized rods implanted within the spine of newborns, before subjecting them to violent shock therapy. Of those children, a few grew capable of harnessing lightning, while many more were crippled for life—a small price to pay for salvation. This very technology was later used to create the Galvanized Prowlers, mortal enemies of the Lightning Vessels, as the Scions started fearing their own creation.

subclassFeature.name: Galvanic Heart
entries: Lightning is part of you. It flows through your veins and awaits release. You gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning damage. If you already have this {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB}, you can reduce the Lightning damage further. To determine the amount reduced, roll a number of {@dice d6}s equal to your Rage Damage bonus and add them together (after the {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} applies).

entries.name: Vessel Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Vessel Damage
entries: Some of your features use Vessel Damage. To determine that extra damage, roll a number of {@dice d4}s equal to your Rage Damage bonus and add them together. Your Vessel Damage is always Lightning damage.

subclassFeature.name: Unbound Storm
entries: While your {@classFeature Rage|Barbarian|XPHB|1|XPHB} is active, you can unleash lightning with the following options.

items.name: Electrified Chains
items.entry: You can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to create chains of lightning that wrap around your weapon. The next time you hit a creature this turn, it takes your Vessel Damage and becomes ensnared by the chains, which anchor to the ground, until the start of your next turn. Each time it attempts to move more than 10 feet while ensnared, it must make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your Vessel save DC, freeing itself on a success. On a failure, it takes your Vessel Damage, and its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fulgurant Strike
items.entry: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack, you can leave the weapon embedded in their chest for a brief moment and immediately take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to call down lightning from the heavens to strike them, using the weapon as a conduit, before retrieving it. The target takes your Vessel Damage, and each other creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or also take that damage. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

items.name: Lightning Step
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can move up to half your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}. During this rush, your body becomes supercharged; if you end this movement within 5 feet of a creature, it takes your Vessel Damage as the lightning leaps to them. If there are multiple creatures, choose one that takes the damage.

subclassFeature.name: Roaring Crash
entries: You are ready to leap into battle at a moment's notice, crashing down on your foes like thunder from the heavens. As part of entering your Rage, you can leap into the air and crash down on a space on the ground you can see within 30 feet of yourself that isn't occupied by a Huge or larger creature. Each creature in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the destination space must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking twice your Vessel Damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

If a creature is in the destination space, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the saving throw and is pushed 5 feet out of the space to an unoccupied space of their choice. If no unoccupied space is available within that range, the creature instead has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

When you reach Barbarian level 10, the distance you can leap increases to 60 feet, and you can land in spaces occupied by Huge creatures. When you reach Barbarian level 14, the distance increases to 90 feet, and you can land in spaces occupied by any creature.

subclassFeature.name: Lightning Reflexes
entries: The lightning you wield enhances your reflexes past what your body could normally handle. As a result, whenever you make a Dexterity check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of +1).
In addition, while your Rage is active, you can use your Lightning Step once on each of your turns without taking a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Electric Beast
entries: You are one with the lightning that flows through you. You can add your Constitution modifier to your Vessel Damage, and the options of your Unbound Storm improve in the following ways.

items.name: Electrified Chains
items.entry: An ensnared creature must make the Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check if it attempts to move 5 feet, and on a failure, it can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions} until the start of your next turn.

items.name: Fulgurant Strike
items.entry: The size of the {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} increases to 20 feet, and you can choose a number of creatures equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum one) that automatically succeed on the saving throw.

items.name: Lightning Step
items.entry: When you rush, you can move up to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and you can choose to merge with the lightning, teleporting the distance moved instead.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Symbiosis
entries: The Circle of Symbiosis allows Druids devoted to Nature to become one with it—in the most real sense of the word. These Druids have mastered osteomancy and use it to sever their own limbs and replace them with fragments of the natural world. To become "awakened symbiotic entities", something others would decry as aberrations, they graft one or multiple limbs to their body. Deer hind-legs replace their own, tree branches take over their arms, and the most devoted and zealous replace their head with that of an animal.

By reveling in such powers, the Circle of Symbiosis seeks to make all living beings one with Nature—or else. No sacrifice is too great for the cause. As such, even children of the circle are forced to undergo these often deadly abscissions, developing their rampaging powers soon after and with great affinity. As these Druids age, they become indistinguishable from their grafts, their humanity slowly waning to make way for something more implacable, more unyielding. Their practices have shunned them from most civilized locales, a punishment that hasn't stopped them from recruiting—or abducting—more to join their cause.

subclassFeature.name: Circle of Symbiosis Spells
entries: When you reach a Druid level specified in the Circle of Symbiosis Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Circle of Symbiosis Spells
rows: {@spell Arm Cannon|SGEHPP}, {@spell Calcified Memories|SGEHPP}, {@spell Fractured Shell|SGEHPP}, {@spell Phalangeal Shot|SGEHPP}, {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB}

subclassFeature.name: Grafted Powers
entries: The multiple aspects of Nature that you forcefully implanted within you manifest themselves in other aspects of your life. You gain one of the following options of your choice.

items.name: Bear Back
items.entry: You count as one size larger when determining your carrying capacity and whether you can grapple a creature. In addition, you can add your Wisdom modifier to any Strength check that you make.

items.name: Deer Head
items.entry: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks.

items.name: Goat Hooves
items.entry: You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. You gain a {@variantrule Climb Speed|XPHB} equal to your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}.

entries: These elements can be visible or not, or they can be represented by other natural aspects. Choose at your discretion when you gain this feature.

subclassFeature.name: Wickerbone Behemoth
entries: You can unleash the vicious natural powers held amidst your flesh. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while you aren't wearing armor or holding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your Wild Shape to awaken Nature's anger and turn into a behemoth. A deer skull, wooden skin, goat hooves, or other such natural gifts overtake your body. For the next 10 minutes, or until you use your {@classFeature Wild Shape|Druid|XPHB|2|XPHB} feature, you gain the following benefits:

items: Each arm counts as a {@item Club|XPHB} under the effect of the {@spell Shillelagh|XPHB} spell, and you can use their mastery property. You can otherwise use your hands normally to manipulate objects or cast spells, but you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand|XPHB}) checks made with them.
You are under the effect of the {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} spell (no {@status Concentration|XPHB} required).

Whenever a creature damages you with an attack, your skin splinters and each creature of your choice within 5 feet of you takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage. Starting at Druid level 10, this damage increases to {@damage 2d4}.

The stress of battle stimulates your organism to fight and survive. At the start of each of your turns, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to half the damage taken since the start of your previous turn, up to a maximum of five times your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}. This regeneration doesn't work if you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.

subclassFeature.name: Extra Attack
entries: You can attack twice, instead of once, whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn. Moreover, you can cast one of your cantrips in place of one of those attacks.

subclassFeature.name: Nature's Wrath
entries: Your natural grafts succumb to your osteomantic powers and allow you to tap deeper into Nature's fury. You are permanently under the effect of the {@spell Barkskin|XPHB} spell.

In addition, while your Wickerbone Behemoth feature is active, your size is Large, and whenever you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Bludgeoning, Piercing and Slashing damage until the end of your next turn. You lose those {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances} early if you take Fire damage.

subclassFeature.name: Briarheart
entries: Your fusion is complete, and your heart is absorbed, its sacrifice making way for a new heart—one that can fully channel the rage of the natural world. While you are a behemoth of your Wickerbone Behemoth feature, you can use the {@itemMastery Nick} mastery property in addition to the {@itemMastery Slow} mastery property with your arms.

In addition, if you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to cast any {@filter Osteomancy spell|spells|components & miscellaneous=|subschool=osteomancy|cast time=action}{@sup *} that has a casting time of an action.

{@note {@sup *}Osteomancy Spells: {@spell Arm Cannon|SGEHPP}, {@spell Brittle Bone Throw|SGEHPP}, {@spell Calcified Memories|SGEHPP}, {@spell Displacing Maw|SGEHPP}, {@spell Dread Scarecrow|SGEHPP}, {@spell Forest of Dread|SGEHPP}, {@spell Fractured Shell|SGEHPP}, {@spell Maiden of Bones|SGEHPP}, {@spell Marrow Transplant|SGEHPP}, {@spell Osseous Impalement|SGEHPP}, {@spell Phalangeal Shot|SGEHPP}, {@spell Skeletal Tail|SGEHPP}}

subclassFeature.name: Blood Hound
entries: Blood Hounds are cursed beings that should not exist. Birthed from nightmarish experiments by the Obitus Scholare, these hunters use a cursed method of fighting, weaving their own blood into attacks to produce supernatural effects. Their powers come from tarblood, an amalgamation of hundreds of species' blood that was forcefully injected in the veins of hunters. Those who didn't die or go insane during the procedure became the first Blood Hounds; only they and their descendants can wield this vicious power.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Strike
entries: You learn to unleash the destructive properties of your blood. When you gain this feature, you learn three {@filter Blood Strike|optionalfeatures|feature type=bs} options of your choice.

Once per turn when you make a weapon attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can apply one of your Blood Strike options to that attack. You can decide to use the option before or after the attack hits, unless the option doesn't involve an attack roll. When you use a Blood Strike, you take Necrotic damage equal to one roll of its Blood Cost. This damage can't be reduced or prevented in any way. A Blood Strike is considered a magical effect.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to 1 + your Constitution modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

You learn an additional Blood Strike option of your choice when you reach Fighter levels 5, 9, 13, and 17. Each time you learn a new Blood Strike option, you can also replace one Blood Strike you know with a different one.

entries.name: Blood Strike Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Constitution modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Blood Strike Options
entries: The Blood Strike feature lets you choose options at certain levels, which are presented here in alphabetical order. These options use your Blood Strike save DC.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Hound Anatomy
entries: Your body adapts to the tarblood within. You are immune to magical contagions, have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Poison damage, and have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws to avoid or end the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition.

In addition, once you've fought a creature, you can relentlessly track it, sensing the blood of your prey. You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Intelligence ({@skill Investigation|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check you make to find a creature to which you have dealt damage and that has blood.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Armament
entries: While you are wielding a weapon and do not have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition, that weapon is considered blood-coated. Such a weapon can deal your choice of Acid, Necrotic, or Poison damage instead of its normal damage type.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Explosion
entries: When you make an attack roll with a blood-coated weapon and miss, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to detonate the blood. The target and each creature other than you in a 5-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes damage as if it were hit by the weapon. On a successful save, a target takes half damage.

subclassFeature.name: Blood of Creation
entries: You further your insight into the tarblood within yourself. You gain the following benefits:

items: When you roll the Blood Cost of a Blood Strike you can reroll the result and choose the lower number.
Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}, you can replace one Blood Strike option you know with a different one.

subclassFeature.name: Blood Symphony
entries: All are unmade by the blood. Whenever you use a Blood Strike, you regain {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum 1). In addition, if the target dies within 1 minute of being damaged by a Blood Strike, you regain one expended use of your Blood Strike feature.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Blood Strike
entries: Your Blood Strike options improve, noted in each option's description.

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Eldritch Hunt
entries: The Oath of the Eldritch Hunt is sworn to the eradication of the unnatural, the aberrant, and the alien. These hunters tread a fine line, enhancing themselves with their prey's powers whilst trying to maintain their own sanity. Unfortunately, this frenzied hunger drives many to madness, and it is no rare occurrence for these Paladins to have to hunt their own.

This oath is found most frequently among Paladins of the Radiant Order. Erroneously nicknamed grey templars, witch hunters, and knights aberrant, these oft-deformed warriors devote themselves to obliterating the Scourge and its creations.

entries.subclassFeature: Tenets of the Eldritch Hunt|Paladin|XPHB|Eldritch Hunt|SGEHPP|3|SGEHPP
Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells|Paladin|XPHB|Eldritch Hunt|SGEHPP|3|SGEHPP

entries.name: Resolve
entries: Through willpower and tenacity, the strain of the hunt is endured; aching limbs and ailing minds are no reason to fall short.

entries.name: Respect
entries: Take life only when doing so protects others. Kill only when necessary, lest the bloodshed enamour your soul and hunter becomes beast.

entries.name: Responsibility
entries: Many rely on your talent to survive the moonlit nights. No matter the circumstances, do not fail them. Sacrifice your own body so that others can retain the sanctity of their own, untainted forms.

subclassFeature.name: Hunt the Prey
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can expend one use of your {@classFeature Channel Divinity|Paladin|XPHB|3|XPHB} to call upon the sanctified hunt. You designate a creature within 60 feet of you as your prey, marking the target for 1 minute. When you use this feature, and as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} on subsequent turns, you can magically teleport up to 60 feet to an unoccupied space you can see within 5 feet of the marked target. To teleport in this way, you must be able to see the marked target.
If the creature drops to 0 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} before the feature ends, you can transfer the mark to a different creature within 60 feet of yourself (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells
entries: The magic of your oath ensures you always have certain spells ready; when you reach a Paladin level specified in the Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

entries.caption: Oath of the Eldritch Hunt Spells
rows: {@spell Evard's Black Tentacles|XPHB}, {@spell Maiden of Bones|SGEHPP}

subclassFeature.name: Stolen Eldritch Gift
entries: Your body is enhanced beyond mortal limits. You can add your Charisma modifier to any {@skill Athletics|XPHB}, {@skill Perception|XPHB}, and {@skill Survival|XPHB} checks that you make.

subclassFeature.name: Sharpened Senses
entries: You have learned to read your prey to find their flaws. When a creature is in your Aura of Protection, you learn any {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immunities}, {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB|Resistances}, or {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB|Vulnerabilities} that it has.
In addition, you have {@sense Blindsight|XPHB} within the range of your Aura of Protection.

subclassFeature.name: Relentless Pursuit
entries: When you hit your marked target with a Melee weapon or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} immediately after you teleport with the Hunt the Prey feature, you can cast {@classFeature Divine Smite|Paladin|XPHB|2|XPHB} without using a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You expend a spell slot as normal, and you can cast this spell in this way only once per turn.

subclassFeature.name: Perfect Hunter
entries: You are the embodiment of the eldritch hunt; none can get in the way of your kill. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you activate the power of the true hunter. For the next 10 minutes, you gain the following benefits:

items.name: Devour
items.entry: Your weapon attacks deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Necrotic damage. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} and {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Necrotic damage.

items.name: Sunder
items.entry: You are Immune to the {@condition Grappled|XPHB}, {@condition Paralyzed|XPHB}, and {@condition Restrained|XPHB} conditions.

items.name: Vanish
items.entry: You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.

entries: Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can also restore your use of it by expending a level 5 spell slot (no action required).

subclassFeature.name: Torturer Conclave
entries: Enshrouded within the radiance of Luyarnha, a conclave of Rangers lies concealed, their solemn duty vowed to the preservation of peace within the walls, regardless of the means. Ever vigilant against the insidious advance of the Scourge, they have honed their inquisitorial craft, recognizing the importance of early prevention of this plague. They achieve this by finding and interrogating victims—and even potential victims—before signs of sickness manifest themselves.

Although these Rangers have been known to serve the clergy and royalty, since the fall of the House of Commons, they are no longer beholden to the fickle desires of any specific lord or lady. Many are now driven by a loftier purpose, one that necessitates the utmost discipline and commitment, for they recognize that if the Scourge is allowed to propagate, it shall wreak havoc upon all they cherish. Yet, some pursue baser ambitions, offering their expertise to those who desire to bend these Rangers to their malevolent will, extracting confessions or inflicting retribution upon adversaries. After all, torture, a practice as ancient as the very bedrock of the earth, is a dreadful instrument, potent enough to shatter even the most indomitable of spirits.

In the throes of battle, these Rangers bring their torturous expertise with them, employing it with merciless precision to break their enemies and methodically subject them to unspeakable agony. They show no mercy to their foes, for they are well aware that none would be extended to them in kind.

entries.name: Disclaimer
entries: Please be advised that while some may use torture as a plot device or as a means of gathering information, it is a sensitive and disturbing topic. While the use of torture can be integral to the story being told, which is why it is included in this book, it is important to ensure that everyone at the table comes to an agreement regarding its use prior to the session beginning, and if it's included, whether descriptions should fade to black or be more detailed.

subclassFeature.name: Tools of the Trade
entries: You've learned to interrogate and use implements of torture. You gain proficiency with {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} and the {@skill Insight|XPHB} skill. You also have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} with them.

subclassFeature.name: Torturer Techniques
entries: You learn to use techniques. Unlike others who require patience and careful preparation, you make use of techniques that are fueled by your magic, letting you employ of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in the midst of hunts—no creature too alien or too resolute to escape your methods.

You can use each technique twice, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. You can expend one use of your {@classFeature Favored Enemy|Ranger|XPHB|1|XPHB} feature (no action required) to regain one use of a technique.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: When you hit a creature with a melee weapon attack or an {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB} while you have {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} in one hand (or a free hand and the presence of {@item Torture Tools|SGEHPP} at your disposal, such as strapped around your leg), as part of that attack, you can use a technique to enhance it in some way. You can only use a technique once per turn, though you can use different techniques in the same turn, and you can only use one technique per attack.

entries.name: Empowered Techniques
entries: When you use a technique, you can empower it by expending a spell slot (no action required). When you do so, you inflict extra damage to the target, and the target subtracts a number of {@dice d4}s from the saving throws it makes against the technique. The amount of damage and the number of dice subtracted are determined by the level of the spell slot expended, as shown on the following table. You can expend a spell slot up to a level determined by your Ranger level, also shown on the following table. You can also empower a technique if you expend one use of your Favored Enemy feature, which counts as a level 1 spell slot.

entries.name: Techniques
entries: You learn each of the following techniques. At higher levels, these techniques are improved.

entries.name: Technique Save DC
entries: If a technique requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Combing
entries: You scrape, tear, and flay the victim's body. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d10} Slashing damage.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if you damage a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it begins to decompose, taking Necrotic damage equal to your Wisdom modifier at the start of each of its turns for 1 minute. This damage can't be reduced or prevented. The creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.
Any extra damage from empowering this technique also applies to this Necrotic damage. A creature can't suffer multiple instances of this effect at once.

entries.name: Enucleation
entries: You aim a vicious strike at the target's eye, reducing their vision to a macabre blur. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} of the weapon's damage type, and it must make a Constitution saving throw. Creatures with more than two eyes have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. On a failed save, the target has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks and has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition against anything further than 60 feet from it for 1 minute. The target repeats this save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it has the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition for the same duration.

entries.name: Hamstringing
entries: You slash at the creature's tendons. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} reduced to 0 until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Nerve Scraping
entries: You damage the creature's nerves. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d4} Psychic damage and must make a Constitution saving throw.

On a failed save, until the start of your next turn, the target must use its action before moving to make a melee attack against a randomly determined creature within reach other than itself. If no creature is in reach, it acts normally but randomly determines targets.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if the target fails this save two rounds in a row, it subtracts {@dice 1d4} from its attack rolls and saving throws for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on a success.

entries.name: Throat Chop
entries: You deliver a fierce cleave to the target's throat, severely impairing its ability to breathe and speak. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and can't speak or use the Verbal components of spells until the start of your next turn.

Starting at Ranger level 11, if you hit a target two rounds in a row with this technique, it must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has the {@condition Stunned|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

entries.name: Tympanic Rupture
entries: You slam the target's ears in an attempt to destabilize it. On a hit, the target takes an extra {@damage 1d8} Bludgeoning damage and must succeed on a Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Deafened|XPHB} condition for 1 minute. A {@condition Deafened|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.

Starting at Ranger level 7, if the target fails its saving throw against this technique two rounds in a row, it is disoriented for the duration. While disoriented, the target can't take {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB|Reactions}.

subclassFeature.name: Depraved Mind
entries: You've seen the worst depravities that plague this world and have committed most of them. You are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition and gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Psychic damage.

In addition, if a creature attempts to read your mind or telepathically talk to you against your will, it must first make a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC. On a failed save, it witnesses the horrors within your mind. It takes Psychic damage equal to your level and fails to communicate with you. On a successful save, it can interact with you in this way for 1 minute without making the saving throw.

subclassFeature.name: Veil of Pain
entries: When you damage a creature with your torturer techniques, you can attempt to rattle its mind with the pain (no action required). The target must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your Technique save DC or start dissociating your presence, its mind refusing to acknowledge the anguish you are causing it, only perceiving you as a flicker. You have the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition to the target for 1 minute. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success.
You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum once) and regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Mental Agony
entries: You know how to cause pain to your quarry both physically and mentally. When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that failed a saving throw against one of your torturer techniques since the start of your last turn makes an Intelligence, a Wisdom, or a Charisma saving throw, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to flourish your blades, smile, or perform a similar terrifying display. The target subtracts {@dice 1d10} from its saving throw. Creatures that are immune to the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition are immune to this effect.

subclassFeature.name: Blade of Radiance
entries: The Blades of Radiance, also called Steel Saints, are known to be one of the most lethal orders of the Church. In order to become a blade, one must be a devout follower of the faith, as only those who would die for the cause are deemed worthy. Prospective members are trained within the walls of the Church, taking on the clergy as their new kin and discarding whatever familial bonds they might have held onto. Their zealous fervor grants them unrivaled powers on the battlefield, wielding massive weapons as if they were mere toys, infusing their blade with divine powers, and breaking down their foes one by one.

The Blades of Radiance receive an incredibly diverse range of missions. The most brutal of their members handle gruesome matters in a lethal fashion, whereas those of a more empathetic temperament are tasked with protecting their fellows. Despite this sundry in character, they all share one goal: safeguarding the Church and its members, no matter what.

subclassFeature.name: Sanctified Champion
entries: Your intense training bears fruit. You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and training with Medium armor.

Whenever you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}, you can perform a ritual on a melee weapon you are proficient with that deals Piercing or Slashing damage, sanctifying it. It becomes your sanctified blade, and you can only have one such blade at a time. The blade has the {@itemProperty Finesse|XPHB} property for you, and attacks made with it against Aberrations, Fiends, and Undead ignore {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to damage.

subclassFeature.name: Divine Blessings
entries: Your devotion to eradicating enemies of the Church manifests as righteous power. You have a pool of Divine Points equal to 1 + your Wisdom modifier (minimum of 1 point). You regain all expended points when you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}. In addition, whenever you kill an Aberration, Beast, Fiend, or Undead of CR 1/2 or higher with your sanctified blade, you regain 1 expended Divine Point.

entries.name: Radiance Save DC
entries: If a feature of this subclass requires a saving throw, the DC equals 8 plus your Wisdom modifier and {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.
You can expend Divine Points to use the following features.

items.name: Armor of the Faithful
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature targets you with an attack, you can expend 1 Divine Point to force that creature to make a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, the attacker must choose a new target or the attack has no effect. In addition, the attacker can't target you with an attack until the start of your next turn. This feature doesn't protect you from areas of effect, such as the explosion of a {@spell Fireball|XPHB} spell.

items.name: Divine Inspiration
items.entry: When you make an Intelligence ({@skill History|XPHB} or {@skill Religion|XPHB}) or a Wisdom ({@skill Insight|XPHB}) check, you can expend 1 Divine Point to reroll the {@dice d20}, and you must use the new result. You can choose to use this feature after you roll the die, but before the outcome is determined. You gain a bonus to the check equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

items.name: Rend the Blasphemous
items.entry: On your turn after you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with your sanctified blade, you can take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} and expend 1 Divine Point to let the divine hand guide you. Make a weapon attack with it against a creature within your reach. You gain a bonus to your attack roll equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum 1).

subclassFeature.name: Righteous Armament
entries: Your faith gives you the power to rebel against fate itself. You learn the following features that use your Divine Points.

items.name: Chains of Judgement
items.entry: When you hit a creature with your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to create holy chains around the creature. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or take Radiant damage equal to your Wisdom modifier and have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of your next turn.

items.name: Divine Retaliation
items.entry: As a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} when a creature damages you with a melee attack while you are wielding your sanctified blade, you can expend 1 Divine Point to make a melee attack with your blade against the creature. You gain a bonus to the damage roll equal to your Wisdom modifier.

items.name: Erupting Blades
items.entry: When you hit a creature with an attack that could apply your Sneak Attack damage, you can forgo damaging the creature with your Sneak Attack and expend 2 Divine Points to cause radiant blades to fall on the battlefield. The target and each creature in a 45-foot-long, 5-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} originating from the target must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes Radiant damage equal to your Sneak Attack damage. On a successful save, a target takes half damage.

subclassFeature.name: Saintly Revelations
entries: You experience revelations, showing you how to channel divine energy to embolden your blade. You learn two cantrips of your choice from the {@filter Cleric spell|spells|level=0|class=cleric|components & miscellaneous=|subschool=osteomancy} list.

In addition, you always have the {@spell Heroism|XPHB}, {@spell Protection From Evil and Good|XPHB}, and {@spell Shield of Faith|XPHB} spells prepared. With this feature, you can cast these spells at will, targeting only yourself, without a spell slot or components. Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for these spells.

Starting at Rogue level 17, when you cast these spells using this feature, they don't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}. However, you can only have one spell cast from this feature active at a time; if you cast a second one, the first spell ends.

subclassFeature.name: Final Judgement
entries: Your sanctified blade becomes imbued with holy power, granting you the following benefits.

items.name: Divine Spirits
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action while wielding the blade, you can cast {@spell Spirit Guardians|XPHB} without a spell slot or components. Creatures within the area of the spell, for the purpose of your Sneak Attack, are considered within 5 feet of an ally of yours. Once you cast the spell with this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend 3 Divine Points (no action required) to restore your use of it.

items.name: Radiant Blade
items.entry: You can speak a command word (no action required) to cause your blade to emit {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet. The light lasts until you speak the command word again or you stow your weapon. While emitting light in this way, the weapon is considered a magic weapon, and attacks made with it deal an extra {@damage 2d4} Radiant damage on a hit.

subclassFeature.name: Osteomancer
entries: Osteomancers are powerful Wizards who understand the power that can be harvested from bones. Often said to be cursed and talked about under cover of night, this sort of magic makes the uneducated shiver and the scholar morbidly curious. Those who have the cunning, bravery, or simple foolishness to pursue research in this field find themselves rewarded with afflicted knowledge. These accursed souls are known as Osteomancers.

The abilities of an Osteomancer are unsettling, if not terrifying to most. Due to their focus on manipulating bones, a topic that is cloaked in mystery and taboo, regular folks regard them as cursed and malevolent beings. Those who see their magic at work have compared it to witnessing a puppet master—bending and twisting enemies to their whim. Many people fail to realize that an Osteomancer's favorite puppet is themselves and that they will readily desecrate their own body in order to crush their opponent.

subclassFeature.name: Brittle Bone Armor
entries: You learn the basics of osteomancy, using it for protection. As an action, if you're not wearing armor or wielding a {@item Shield|XPHB}, you can force a frame of bones out of your body to protect you, granting you {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to twice your Wizard level that last for 1 hour.
While you have these {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Piercing and Slashing damage, and you have a +2 bonus to AC.
Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB} unless you expend a spell slot of level 2 or higher (no action required) to restore your use of it.

subclassFeature.name: Anatomical Expert
entries: Your pursuit of osteomancy has required many hours studying the anatomy of a myriad of creatures. You gain proficiency in the {@skill Medicine|XPHB} skill, and when you make a Wisdom ({@skill Medicine|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check, you gain a bonus to the check equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum 1). In addition, when these checks concern a creature that possesses a skeleton, you have {@variantrule Expertise|XPHB} in that skill, even if you don't have proficiency in the {@skill Survival|XPHB} skill.

subclassFeature.name: Bone Puppetry
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you target one creature you can see within 60 feet of you that has a skeleton. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC or you take total and precise control of its skeleton. Until the end of the creature's next turn, it takes only the actions you choose and doesn't do anything that you don't allow it to do. In the creature's efforts to resist your command, attack rolls it makes against its allies have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB}, and its allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws from effects caused by the creature.

You can only have one such creature under your control at a time. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

subclassFeature.name: Skeletal Mastery
entries: You are a master of your own body. You have the following benefits.

items.name: Many Forms
items.entry: You can reshape your bones, including those of your face, to appear as a completely different person. You can cast {@spell Alter Self|XPHB} without expending a spell slot. When you cast this spell using this feature, it doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB}, and you can only use the Change Appearance or Natural Weapons options.

items.name: Skeletal Control
items.entry: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can dissolve or restore your own skeleton. While boneless, you can move yourself through sheer muscular and magical control. In this form, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 10 feet, and you can move through a space as narrow as 1 inch without squeezing. Further, you are considered as having the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, can't use your hands, and can't attack or cast spells. As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can regenerate the bones in your hands to exert finer control over them until the end of your next turn.

subclassFeature.name: Improved Bone Puppetry
entries: You've enhanced your mastery over skeletal manipulation. When a creature fails its saving throw against your Bone Puppetry feature, your control of the target lasts for 1 minute. The target can't resist your command; it doesn't have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on attacks against its allies, nor do its allies have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against effects caused by the target. The target repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. You must concentrate on this feature as you would concentrate on a spell, and damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

Once under your control, when the target repeats the saving throw against your Bone Puppetry, you can choose to expend one additional use of the feature to give the creature {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on the save. You must decide to do so before seeing the result of the roll.

optionalfeature.name: Bewitching Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d8}

You infuse fey blood into your attack. A creature hit by this attack takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Psychic damage and must make a Wisdom saving throw. If it fails the save, you can choose one of the target's allies within 30 feet of it; the target now considers that ally as an enemy until the start of your next turn.
The Psychic damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Bloodboil Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d6}

You infuse your attack with fiendish blood, which detonates when it mixes with another creature's blood. When you hit a creature, the target and each creature other than you in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target take {@damage 2d6} Fire damage and start burning. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.
The Fire damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Bloodshard Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d6}

You infuse your attack with fiendish blood, which detonates when it mixes with another creature's blood. When you hit a creature, the target and each creature other than you in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target take {@damage 2d6} Fire damage and start burning. This damage ignores {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Fire damage.
The Fire damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Bloodshard Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d8}

You unleash a thread of sharp blood from your weapon, which, instead of an attack roll, fires forward in a 1-foot-wide, 60-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line}, before disappearing. The blood passes harmlessly through objects, ignoring {@variantrule Cover|XPHB}. Each creature in that {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} makes a Dexterity saving throw, taking damage as if it were hit by the weapon plus an extra {@damage 1d6} Piercing damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.
The Piercing damage increases to {@damage 3d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Constraining Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d8}

When this attack strikes a creature, blood tainted by oozes creates grasping and sharp tendrils of blood, which wrap around the target. The target takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Acid damage, it has {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on its next attack roll, and it must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 2d6} Acid damage the first time on each of its turns that it moves 5 feet or more without teleporting. A creature can use an action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your Blood Strike save DC, removing the tendrils and ending the effect on itself or another creature within its reach on a success. Otherwise, the tendrils last for 1 minute or until you use this option again.
Both Acid damages increase to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Exiling Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d10}

You use celestial blood to try to temporarily banish your target to a harmless location in the Celestial Plane. A creature hit by the attack must succeed on a Charisma saving throw or be banished. While banished in this way, its {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 and it has the {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} condition. At the end of its next turn, the target reappears in the space it left or in the nearest unoccupied space if that space is occupied.
When you reach Fighter level 18, the target also takes {@damage 2d6} Radiant damage when the attack hits it.

optionalfeature.name: Hunting Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d4}

Using ancient bestial blood, you grant your strikes unparalleled precision. Your next attack roll ignores benefits to {@variantrule Armor Class|XPHB} granted by Shields, armor, or magical effects, such as the {@spell Shield|XPHB} or {@spell Mage Armor|XPHB} spells. When you hit a creature with this attack, it takes an extra {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage, and for the next minute, you know the target's exact location, and it doesn't gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attacks against you as a result of having the {@condition Invisible|XPHB} condition.
The Slashing damage increases to {@damage 3d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Shadowblood Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d6}

You weave threads of shadows from the blood of your foe, causing it to obscure the battlefield. A creature hit by the attack takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage, and its blood forms a dark red mist of magical {@spell Darkness|XPHB} spreads in a 10-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from the target until the start of your next turn. {@sense Darkvision|XPHB} can't see through this {@spell Darkness|XPHB}, and nonmagical light can't illuminate it.
The Necrotic damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Thunderblood Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d4}

You imbue your attack with forceful energy drawn from the blood of giants. The attack detonates, and a creature hit by this attack takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Thunder damage and is pushed 15 feet straight away. In addition, the target must succeed on a Strength saving throw or have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.
The Thunder damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

optionalfeature.name: Withering Strike
entries: {@b Blood Cost:} {@dice 1d6}

You weave cursed undead blood into your attack. A creature hit by the attack takes an extra {@damage 2d6} Necrotic damage and must make a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, damage dealt by the target's attacks is halved until the start of your next turn.
The Necrotic damage increases to {@damage 4d6} when you reach Fighter level 18.

item.name: Torture Tools
entries: This satchel contains various small implements that can bludgeon, cut, and pierce in ways designed to maximize pain. Meant to extract the truth, many use these tools with far more nefarious intentions.
Proficiency with these tools grants the following benefits:

entries.name: Exhaustion
entries: Using these tools for 1 hour on a {@condition Restrained} creature causes it to gain 1 {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB} level, after which you must make a Dexterity (Torture Tools) check. The DC is equal to 20 minus the creature's Constitution modifier. On a failure, the creature takes 10 points of your choice of Bludgeoning, Piercing, or Slashing damage.

entries.name: Intimidation
entries: When you make a Charisma ({@skill Intimidation}) check against a creature you have previously used these tools on, you gain a bonus to the roll equal to twice your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

item.name: Sacrificial Brand (Drawn)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Drawn (Common)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving.

item.name: Sacrificial Brand (Tattooed)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Tattooed (Uncommon)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them.

item.name: Sacrificial Brand (Scarified)
entries: The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Scarified (Rare)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them, and they have a -3 penalty to attack rolls and damage rolls against other creatures not bearing the brand.

In addition, creatures bearing this carving begin to painfully bleed from it when {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} monsters within 300 feet of them are aware of their position. They can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB} for the duration of the Blood Moon.

item.name: Meat Hookshot
entries: When the {@race Manikin|SGEHPP} of the Sloered Abattoir gained sentience, the Scions sent enforcers to quell this threat to Luyarnha's delicate existence. From the abattoir's meat hooks and the blunderbusses of the slain enforcers, The Slaughtered—as the manikins named themselves—crafted these versatile weapons. Nicknamed "the meat hook", the hookshot is a trick weapon used by hunters to help close the gap to their prey in a devastating whirl of blades and gunpowder.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the hookshot is two one-handed weapons connected by a short length of chain: a {@item Sickle|XPHB} and a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a single two-handed weapon: a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} with a bladed attachment that can act as a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB}.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: While Untransformed, the {@item Sickle|XPHB} has the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property, and the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} doesn't have the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property. Using this pair of weapons together requires the {@item Sickle|XPHB} to be held in one hand and the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} in the other. When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with the {@item Sickle|XPHB}, you can make an attack with the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, ignoring the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Bar|SGEHPP|Barrel} property.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can attack with either the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} or the bladed attachment (which uses the stats of a {@item Battleaxe|XPHB} wielded with two hands). In addition, this item gains the Hookshot property.

entries.name: Hookshot
entries: As a {@action Utilize|XPHB} action, you can launch the sickle from the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}, to which it remains attached by a length of sturdy chain. Make a ranged attack roll against a creature you can see within 30 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes Slashing damage equal to {@damage 1d4} plus your Dexterity modifier. If the creature is your size or smaller, it must succeed on a {@dc 13} Strength saving throw or be pulled in a straight line to the nearest unoccupied space to you. If the creature is larger than you, you are pulled in a straight line to the nearest unoccupied space to it. At the end of your turn, the hook detaches from the creature and reattaches itself to the {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP}.

item.name: Dream Executioner

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the Dream Executioner is a {@item Scythe|SGEHPP} and a lantern. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a single massive {@item Maul|XPHB}.
You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The {@item Scythe|SGEHPP} gains the Harvest property.

entries.name: Harvest
entries: Whenever a creature of CR 1 or higher (or level 1 or higher) dies within 15 feet of you, the lantern harvests the creature's soul. The soul becomes trapped in the lantern, and the creature can't be resurrected until the soul is freed. As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can free a soul trapped in the lantern. The lantern can hold a maximum of one soul.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: The {@item Maul|XPHB} gains the Soul Explosion property.

entries.name: Soul Explosion
entries: When you hit a creature with this weapon while a soul is held in the lantern, you can sacrifice the soul, permanently destroying it, to create a massive explosion of ghostflame. Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a {@dc 14} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 2d8} Radiant damage and {@damage 2d8} Necrotic damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Undead automatically fail the saving throw.

item.name: Ravenous Gazer
entries: Acquiring forbidden knowledge always comes at a cost. Any creature that attunes to this glaive is considered proficient with it. You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the gazer is a {@item Glaive|XPHB}. In its Transformed state, the gazer is a {@item Glaive|XPHB} that can be used as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

To transform this weapon, you must feed it your blood: each time you shift this weapon into its Transformed state, or start your turn with the weapon in its Transformed state, you take {@damage 1d4} Necrotic damage, which can't be reduced or prevented in any way. This damage can't break your {@status Concentration|XPHB}.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: While the weapon is in its Transformed state, it grants you a +2 bonus to spell attack rolls, increases your spell save DC by 1, and gives you {@sense Truesight|XPHB} with a range of 30 feet.

item.name: Unstable Crumbler
entries: While holding this weapon, your attacks and spells deal double damage to structures, and Fire damage you take is reduced by an amount equal to your Constitution modifier (minimum of 1).

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, this weapon is a roaring {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} with smoke coming out of its mouth. In its Transformed state, the handle extends, turning the weapon into a highly unstable and destructive {@item Maul|XPHB}. As part of this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can do the following:

items: When you transform the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} into a {@item Maul|XPHB}, you can shoot at your feet, even if the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} isn't loaded, using the deflagration to propel yourself and jump up to 30 feet in any direction. This jump doesn't cost you any movement.

When you transform the {@item Maul|XPHB} into a {@item Cannon|SGEHPP}, you can reload the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} and retain its unstable force. If you reload it in this way, the next time you hit with a ranged attack with the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} on your turn, you are pushed back 30 feet in a straight line.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The Unstable Crumbler heats up {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP|Cannonballs}, transforming them into infernal ammunition. Whenever you roll a 15 or higher on the {@dice d20} when making a ranged attack roll with this weapon, the {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP} becomes overheated and explodes on impact. When the {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP} explodes in this way, it is considered an {@item Explosive Cannonball|SGEHPP}.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: Whenever you roll an 18 or higher on the {@dice d20} when making an attack roll with this weapon, the {@item Maul|XPHB}'s head detonates, causing an effect that acts as the {@spell Fireball} spell (save {@dc 15}) centered on the target. If you succeed on this saving throw, you take no damage.

item.name: Galvanized Claw
entries: While attuned to this weapon, you have {@variantrule Resistance|XPHB} to Lightning and Thunder damage.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the claw is a sinewy leather gauntlet, made from the muscle and hide of a galvanized prowler. In its Transformed state, the claw surges with electrical energy, merging with its wearer's forearm and turning into a monstrous claw.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The bestial hide invigorates you, giving you the lightning fast reflexes of the galvanized prowler slaughtered to make this gauntlet; you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on {@variantrule Initiative|XPHB} rolls. In addition, this gauntlet feeds off of your power. If you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} when you hit with a melee attack, you deal an extra {@damage 1d6} Lightning damage.

The gauntlet has 3 charges and regains all expended charges daily at dawn. When you take Lighting or Thunder damage, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} and expend 1 charge to instead take no damage and gain a number of {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage you would have taken.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: The gauntlet merges with your form, turning your hand into an aberrant claw that you can't be disarmed of. This claw changes the damage of your {@variantrule Unarmed Strike|XPHB|Unarmed Strikes} to {@damage 1d8}, the damage type to Slashing, and you can use your Dexterity or Strength modifier for the attack rolls and damage rolls made with it. Further, you gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with it.

When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action with this claw, you can make one attack with it as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. In addition, if you have {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB}, when you hit with a melee attack using this claw, you deal an extra {@damage 1d8} Lightning damage.
The claw is too unwieldy to use for delicate handling, such as activating intricate mechanisms (like the trigger of a firearm) or picking locks with {@item Thieves' Tools|XPHB}.

item.name: Orphan's Cradle
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In both states, the weapon is a {@item Morningstar|XPHB} with the {@itemProperty R|XPHB|Reach} property.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The flowers growing in the cradle exude a sickly sweet scent that calms the mind of men and chases away nightmares. Humanoids within 10 feet of the cradle have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on saving throws against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} and {@condition Frightened|XPHB} conditions. In addition, the cradle has the Cleansing Miasma and Vile Miasma properties.

entries.name: Cleansing Miasma
entries: As a {@action Magic|XPHB} action, you can cleanse one Humanoid you can see within 10 feet of you. It gains {@dice 1d12} {@variantrule Temporary Hit Points|XPHB} and can end one of the following conditions: {@condition Charmed|XPHB}, {@condition Frightened|XPHB}, or {@condition Poisoned|XPHB}. Once a creature has benefited from this property, it can't benefit from it again for 1 hour.

entries.name: Vile Miasma
entries: When you hit a Beast or an Undead with this weapon, the target must succeed on a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw or have the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition for 1 minute, even if the target is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to the {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} condition. A {@condition Poisoned|XPHB} creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Vile Miasma for the next 24 hours.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: When Transformed, the cradle's plants ignite, and it deals an extra {@damage 2d6} Fire damage on a hit. In addition, the weapon gains the Fanned Flames and Withering Flames properties.

entries.name: Fanned Flames
entries: As an action, you can rotate the cradle wildly around you, fanning the flames. Each creature in a 20-foot Cone must make a {@dc 16} Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 3d6} Fire damage and {@damage 3d6} Poison damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one. Beasts and Undead have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on this saving throw. After this property is used, Orphan's Cradle reverts to its Untransformed state and can't be Transformed again for {@dice 1d4} rounds.

entries.name: Withering Flames
entries: When you hit a Beast or an Undead with this weapon, you can force the target to make a {@dc 16} Constitution saving throw. On a failure, the target has {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to your choice of one of the following damage types until the start of its next turn: Acid, Cold, Fire, Lightning, Poison, or Radiant. If a creature's saving throw is successful or the effect ends for it, the creature is {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to Withering Flames for the next 24 hours.

item.name: Revelations
item.reqAttune: by a creature with a Strength of 15 or higher
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While attuned to it, your sight improves as your vision starts echoing with that of the blade. While holding Revelations, you gain the following benefits:

items: You can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB}.
Other creatures don't gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on attack rolls against you as a result of being unseen by you.
You are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|immune} to the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, as the sword absorbs the effect and closes two of its eyes instead, before regrowing them.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the weapon is a {@item Cleaver|SGEHPP} studded with eyeballs. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a {@item Whip|XPHB} composed of metal shards held together by a sinew of blood and flesh.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: When you hit a creature with this {@item Cleaver|SGEHPP}, you curse them for the next hour. For the duration, you gain a +1 bonus to damage rolls made with the weapon against the target, attack rolls you make with the weapon against the cursed target score a {@variantrule Critical Hit|XPHB} on a roll of 19 or 20 on the {@dice d20}, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on any Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB} or {@skill Survival|XPHB}) check you make to find the target. The curse ends early if you transform the weapon or if you have the {@condition Unconscious|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: This {@item Whip|XPHB} deals {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage on a hit, has the {@itemProperty V|XPHB|Versatile} ({@damage 1d8}) property, but does not have the {@itemProperty F|XPHB|Finesse} property. Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with this weapon, you can attempt to crush them under the weight of the {@item Whip|XPHB}. The target must succeed on a Strength saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Strength modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take {@damage 1d6} Slashing damage and have the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition.

entries.name: Curse: Devour Sight
entries: While attuned to this weapon, your sight deteriorates rapidly. For each five days that pass, you gain a permanent -1 penalty to all Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made using your sight. When this penalty reaches -5, your eyes rot and melt out. You have the {@condition Blinded|XPHB} condition, as two new eyes appear on the blade.

The sword's curse is insidious: while you remain attuned to the weapon, you do not suffer the penalty to your {@skill Perception|XPHB} checks, and you do not realize that your sight is worsening. The blade's influence makes you perceive the world in a clearer light.

item.name: Shard of Moonlight
entries: While attuned to this weapon, you gain the following benefits:

items: You are proficient with Greatswords and Longswords.
You gain a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls made with this magic weapon, and the blade deals an extra {@damage 1d6} Radiant damage on a hit.
You have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom saving throws, except those made to resist Madness.
You can use this weapon as a {@variantrule Spellcasting Focus|XPHB}.

entries.name: Sentience
entries: The Shard of Moonlight is a sentient weapon, with the same personality as the Great One whose flesh it was carved from. The weapon sporadically communicates telepathically with its wielder through images and sounds, though it doesn't speak.

entries.name: Trick Weapon
entries: As a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, you can switch between the Transformed and Untransformed states of this weapon. In its Untransformed state, the shard is a metallic {@item Longsword|XPHB} that absorbs light. In its Transformed state, the weapon is a {@item Greatsword|XPHB} that pulses with lunar energy. In both states, this weapon has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property.

entries.name: Untransformed
entries: The blade seems to guide your strikes. Once on each of your turns when you make an attack with this weapon, you can immediately make a second attack (no action required). It has the Void Absorption property.

entries.name: Void Absorption
entries: The void that fills the blade is capable of absorbing magic. While holding the shard, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to absorb a spell that is targeting you, including spells with an area of effect. The absorbed spell's effect is canceled, and the spell's energy—not the spell itself—is stored in the shard in the form of charges. The number of charges gained is equivalent to the level of the spell when it was cast (1 charge for cantrips). The shard can absorb and store up to 10 charges. If the shard doesn't have enough empty charges for a spell, it fails to absorb it. The shard regains all charges each time the moon changes.

entries.name: Transformed
entries: To transform the blade, you must take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} while under direct moonlight. The transformation lasts for 1 minute, or until you end it early as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. While the blade is Transformed, the extra Radiant damage it deals on a hit increases from {@damage 1d6} to {@damage 2d6}, and you can expend the charges stored within the shard. When the shard loses all charges, the transformation ends.
Each time you make an attack in the Transformed state, you can expend charges to create special effects:

entries.name: Revealing Glow
entries: As part of making an attack, you can expend 1 charge to empower the blade. On a hit, it deals an extra {@damage 1d12} Radiant damage, and until the start of your next turn, the target sheds {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} in a 10-foot radius. While affected by the light, the target can't have the {@condition Invisible} condition, and attack rolls against it have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB}.

entries.name: Transient Moonlight
entries: As part of making an attack, you can expend 2 charges to release a wave of moonlight where the blade slashes, creating a 5-foot-wide, 60-foot-long {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} of moonlight originating from you. Each creature in the area must make a {@dc 18} Constitution saving throw, taking {@damage 2d12} Radiant damage on a failed save or half as much damage on a successful one.

entries.name: Lunar Explosion
entries: Instead of making an attack, you can expend 3 charges to raise the blade upward and release a burst of moonlight energy. Each creature in a 30-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you must make a {@dc 18} Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, a target takes {@damage 3d12} Radiant damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. If a creature falls {@condition Prone|XPHB} within 5 feet of you, you can immediately take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to make a melee weapon attack against them with the shard. On a successful save, a target takes half as much damage only.

baseitem.name: Cannonball
entries: A type of Ammunition for weapons with the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Art|SGEHPP|Artillery} property.
Ammunition is required by a weapon that has the {@itemProperty AF|XDMG|Ammunition} property. A weapon's description specifies the type of ammunition used by the weapon.
Firearm ammunition is destroyed upon use.

baseitem.name: Explosive Cannonball
entries: A creature hit by this ammunition takes the weapon's normal damage, and each creature within 10 feet of it must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC 8 plus your Strength modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take {@damage 2d8} Fire damage. On a miss, the ammunition fails to detonate.
Once it hits a target, the ammunition is destroyed.

itemGroup.name: Sacrificial Brand
entries: To apply an Eldritch Carving, one must follow a gruesome process. Unlike most art, where the artist determines the quality of the art, with Eldritch Carvings, the canvas—the person getting carved— determines the quality of the work. The canvas must envision the rune in their mind as best they can, causing their body to distort under the eldritch pressure. The carver can then simply apply the necessary tool against the skin and let the eldritch powers move the brush, needle, or knife, depending on whether the Eldritch Carving is Drawn, Tattooed, or Scarified, respectively. This procedure takes 1 hour and can be done as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

After the Eldritch Carving is complete, a creature is attuned to it (if required) and gains its effects. To remove an Eldritch Carving, the flesh where the Eldritch Carving is located needs to be thoroughly burnt. Burning a carving also removes {@variantrule Attunement|XPHB} to it. Scarified Eldritch Carvings can't be removed.

The carving, notorious among hunters and commonly dubbed the "Brand of Death" is a harbinger of an early demise for those burdened with its curse. Nevertheless, Steinhardt and Martyr Tulio—valiant souls undaunted by fear—carved the eldritch sigil into their own skin willingly. By bearing the ominous symbol, they sought to lure the beasts closer to them during the Hunt, granting their brothers-in-arms moments of respite amidst the chaos.

entries.name: Drawn (Common)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving.

entries.name: Tattooed (Uncommon)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them.

entries.name: Scarified (Rare)
entries: During the three days of the Blood Moon, all Evil-aligned creatures within Luyarnha gain {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) or Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks to locate creatures with this Eldritch Carving. If they are within 120 feet of a creature bearing the Eldritch Carving, they know their exact location and receive a +3 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls against them, and they have a -3 penalty to attack rolls and damage rolls against other creatures not bearing the brand.

In addition, creatures bearing this carving begin to painfully bleed from it when {@variantrule Hostile [Attitude]|XPHB|Hostile} monsters within 300 feet of them are aware of their position. They can't be {@status Surprised|XPHB} for the duration of the Blood Moon.
