itemFluff.name: Galvanized Claw
entries: Ripping the flesh of the beasts they slay to fashion ferocious weapons is something hunters have gotten remarkably good at over the course of their hunts.

itemFluff.name: Revelations
entries: Made of an unknown metal that mixes blood and steel, this ghastly sword is studded with dozens of eyes from various creatures that stare hungrily at all who are confronted with it. Only a competent hunter can wield a weapon of such weight, but armed with it, they will never lose sight of their prey and will never be caught in an ambush. Such a dangerous weapon should only be used with the utmost caution.

itemFluff.name: Shard of Moonlight
entries: This weapon is the flesh of a Great One carved away in pain and fashioned into a blade. The Shard of Moonlight is the reason the Shattered Moon exists and the Devouring Moon is no more. He who wields the blade is overwhelmed by hope, however misguided it might be...

entries.name: Artillery
entries: You must use Strength instead of Dexterity for the attack rolls and damage rolls of a weapon with the Artillery property, and you can use the weapon to make a ranged attack only if you have ammunition to fire from it. The type of ammunition required is specified with the weapon's range. Each attack expends one piece of ammunition. Weapons with the Artillery property must be reloaded with an action. After a fight, you can spend 1 minute to recover half the ammunition (round down) you used in the fight; the rest is lost.

entries.name: Barrel
entries: A Barrel weapon can be fired a number of times equal to the number of bullets its barrel can hold (written as Barrel X) before it must be reloaded. It can be reloaded as either an action or instead of an attack as part of the {@action Attack|XPHB} action. If the weapon also has the {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} property, it can also be reloaded as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}. You must have one free hand to reload the weapon.

entries.name: Blaring
entries: Firing a Blaring weapon makes a thunderous crack. The sound can be heard from up to 100 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it hard to go undetected; you have {@variantrule Disadvantage|XPHB} on Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it has {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Booming
entries: The deflagration from firing a Booming weapon makes a stupendous booming sound. The sound can be heard from up to 500 feet away. Making a ranged attack using a weapon with this property makes it impossible to go undetected; you automatically fail Dexterity ({@skill Stealth|XPHB}) checks made as part of the {@action Hide|XPHB} action until the start of your next turn. In addition, if a creature is within the area of the sound blast, it automatically succeeds on Wisdom ({@skill Perception|XPHB}) checks made against you as part of the {@action Search|XPHB} action.

entries.name: Spread Fire
entries: A weapon that has the Spread Fire property can't make a normal attack. It instead sprays a {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone} with a length equal to its range (for example, a {@item Blunderbuss|SGEHPP} with a range of 20 feet will fire in a 20-foot {@variantrule Cone [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cone}). Each creature in the area must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw (DC equals 8 plus your Dexterity modifier and your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}) or take the weapon's normal damage.

entries.name: Twinned Barrel
entries: A Twinned Barrel weapon has two barrels that can each hold a {@item firearm bullet|XPHB} and can both be loaded as part of reloading the weapon. You can fire both barrels of a Twinned Barrel weapon as part of an attack, instead of each barrel individually. Doing so empties both barrels of the weapon (as per the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Bar|SGEHPP|Barrel} property) and increases the damage die of the weapon on a hit (from {@dice d4} to {@dice d6} to {@dice d8} to {@dice d10} to {@dice d12}).

Unlike most art, where the artist determines the quality of the art, with Eldritch Carvings, the canvas—the person getting carved— determines the quality of the work. The canvas must envision the rune in their mind as best they can, causing their body to distort under the eldritch pressure. The carver can then simply apply the necessary tool against the skin and let the eldritch powers move the brush, needle, or knife, depending on whether the Eldritch Carving is Drawn, Tattooed, or Scarified, respectively. This procedure takes 1 hour and can be done as part of a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB}.

After the Eldritch Carving is complete, a creature is attuned to it (if required) and gains its effects. Scarified Eldritch Carvings can't be removed.

backgroundFluff.name: Beast Hunter
entries: Growing up, the menacing presence of the Scourge loomed over your life in the city. The beasts terrified you, destroyed your homes, and took away people you loved. Driven by vengeance, fear, or a desire for justice, you chose to become a hunter. The Church, a mentor, or the Radiant Order taught you the ways of the hunt, giving you the knowledge and skills needed to defend your city and yourself. Whether you were once a simple citizen turned protector or a seasoned veteran of the First War hardened by countless battles, you have become an essential line of defense against the darkness.

backgroundFluff.name: Inquisitor
entries: You are a steadfast disciple of the Radiant Church, filled with an unwavering faith and a holy zeal that drives you to root out any threats to the Church and its teachings. Your duty might involve questioning potential heretics, investigating signs of corruption within the Church, or combating the enemies of the faith. You walk a fine line, enforcing the laws of the Church and ensuring the purity of its followers.

backgroundFluff.name: Marked for Death
entries: You once were dead, but the mysterious Blood Moon of Rebirth returned you to life, leaving an indelible Eldritch Carving on your body—the Sacrificial Brand. The mark on your flesh is feared by many, as it is believed to attract the terrible creatures that plague the world. To you, it represents the weight of your past life and the promise that this life will again end violently. Embracing your new life as a symbol of rebirth and sacrifice, you have resolved to use this opportunity, even if it leads to countless brutal struggles.

feat.name: Faithful
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Divine Clarity
entries: If you fail a saving throw against the {@condition Charmed|XPHB} or {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you can choose to succeed instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Trial of Faith
entries: Whenever you roll a 1 on a {@variantrule d20 Test|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}.

feat.name: Grizzled
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Overcome
entries: Whenever you make a saving throw against the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition, you gain a bonus to the saving throw equal to your {@variantrule Proficiency|XPHB|Proficiency Bonus}.

entries.name: Survive
entries: You require half as much food and water to survive, and you have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on Wisdom ({@skill Survival|XPHB}) checks made to forage for food and water.

entries.name: Withstand
entries: Immediately after you take damage that causes you to be {@status Bloodied|XPHB}, you gain {@variantrule Heroic Inspiration|XPHB}. You can't gain this benefit again until you finish a {@variantrule Short Rest|XPHB|Short} or {@variantrule Long Rest|XPHB}.

entries.name: Brutal Weaponry
entries: You can wield a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property in one hand, provided your other hand isn't also wielding a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property or holding a {@item Shield|XPHB}.

entries.name: Killing Streak
entries: When you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action on your turn and attack with a weapon that has the {@itemProperty 2H|XPHB|Two-Handed} property, you can make one extra attack as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} later on the same turn. That extra attack must be made with a {@itemProperty L|XPHB|Light} weapon, and you don't add your ability modifier to the extra attack's damage unless that modifier is negative or you have the {@feat Two-Weapon Fighting|XPHB} feat.

feat.name: Cannoneer
entries: You gain the following benefits.

entries.name: Cannon Proficiency
entries: You gain proficiency with {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons}, and you can reload a {@item Cannon|SGEHPP} as a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} instead of an action. You can take this {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} only if you haven't moved during your turn, and after you take the {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB}, your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} is 0 until the end of your turn. Starting at character level 11, this doesn't reduce your {@variantrule Speed|XPHB}, and when you take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action, you can replace one of your attacks with reloading the {@item Cannon|SGEHPP}. When you reach character level 20, you can ignore the {@itemProperty SGEHPP:Art|SGEHPP|Artillery} property of {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons}.

entries.name: Siege
entries: Your attacks with {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons} deal double damage to objects and structures.

entries.name: Strong Back
entries: The weight of {@item Cannon|SGEHPP|Cannons} and {@item Cannonball|SGEHPP|Cannonballs} count as half for you.

spell.name: Brittle Bone Throw
entries: You hurl a splintered bone fragment at a creature within range. Make a ranged spell attack against the target. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} Piercing damage. On a miss, you can shatter the bone mid-air and redirect the remnant towards another creature within 15 feet of the original target. Make another ranged spell attack. On a hit, the new target takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} and {@dice 1d4}, respectively, when you reach levels 5 ({@damage 2d8}, {@damage 2d4}), 11 ({@damage 3d8}, {@damage 3d4}), and 17 ({@damage 4d8}, {@damage 4d4}).

spell.name: Gravity Spike
entries: You create a localized gravitational field that temporarily shifts the landscape to impale a creature. Choose a creature on the ground you can see within range. The creature must make a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, the target takes {@damage 1d4} Piercing damage and has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition. On a successful save, the target takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Cantrip Upgrade
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} when you reach levels 5 ({@damage 2d4}), 11 ({@damage 3d4}), and 17 ({@damage 4d4}).

spell.name: Fractured Shell
entries: You touch a willing creature, forcing spiked bone plates to grow and pierce through its skin. It takes 1 point of Piercing damage. For the duration of the spell, the first time each turn that the target is hit with a melee attack roll, the attacking creature takes {@damage 2d4} Piercing damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d4} for each spell slot level above 1. The spell doesn't require {@status Concentration|XPHB} with a level 5+ spell slot.

spell.name: Phalangeal Shot
entries: You point your fingers forward and your phalangeal bones fire outwards, akin to the bullets of a gun. They regrow immediately, leaving your hand unscathed. All creatures in a 30-foot-long, 1-foot-wide {@variantrule Line [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Line} in front of you must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 2d8} Piercing damage.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Spectral Slash
entries: You send forth a spectral copy of yourself to strike down your foe. Make a melee spell attack against a creature within 20 feet of you. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 1d8} damage of your weapon's damage type.

You can then spend your action to move up to 20 feet in a straight line towards the target, streaking through a spectral trail, and take the {@action Attack|XPHB} action against it. To use this action, you must attack with the melee weapon used for the casting of this spell.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} and the distance traveled by 10 feet for each spell slot level above 1.

spell.name: Arm Cannon
entries: You fire out the bones of your forearm through your hand, leaving a severe wound that immediately regrows and heals. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 4d8} Piercing damage and must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be pushed 15 feet away from you. If pushed into an obstacle, the target is impaled by the bone and has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition until the end of its next turn. Creatures that are Large or larger have {@variantrule Advantage|XPHB} on this saving throw.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8} and the pushing distance by 5 feet for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Blind Ambush
entries: You blow on a whistle, releasing an inaudible sound. Choose a point on the ground within range. The first time a creature moves 5 feet of more while within a 10-foot Square centered on that point before the spell ends, an eldritch maw immediately erupts from beneath the ground, dealing {@damage 2d10} Piercing damage to each creature within the Square and knocking one of them {@condition Prone|XPHB} (decide when the spell triggers). The spell then ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 2. If you use a level 5+ spell slot, the spell can trigger a second time before it ends.

spell.name: Calcified Memories
entries: You touch the bones of a deceased creature. When you do so, a ghostly grey illusion of the fallen creature appears above its corpse to reenact the last 6 seconds of its life. The illusion only shows the creature's actions, such as reacting to an unseen monster or choking from poisonous gas, but does not show the monster or effect causing the behavior, only their outline. This spell has no effect on Undead creatures. Once a corpse's death has been revealed in this way, it can't be shown again for 24 hours.

spell.name: Skeletal Tail
entries: You grow a long, scorpion-like tail made of sharpened bones. Whenever a creature moves while in a 15-foot {@variantrule Emanation [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Emanation} originating from you, you can take a {@variantrule Reaction|XPHB} to try and pierce them with your tail. Make a melee spell attack roll. On a hit the target takes Piercing damage equal to {@damage 2d4} plus your spellcasting modifier and is pulled to an empty space adjacent to you as your tail drags them in.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 2d4} for each spell slot level above 2.

spell.name: Displacing Maw
entries: Your rib cage opens up violently, forming a maw that attempts to devour a creature within range. The creature must make a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 4d8} Piercing damage and is transported through magic to a point of your choice on the ground within 60 feet of you, where the maw reappears and regurgitates them. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d8}, and the teleportation distance increases by 10 feet, for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Osseous Impalement
entries: Massive bone spikes sprout under up to four creatures on the ground of your choice that you can see within range. They must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or take {@damage 3d10} Piercing damage and be impaled by the spike, have the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} condition and be held aloft 5 feet in the air for the duration. A creature {@condition Restrained|XPHB} in this way takes {@damage 1d10} Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns.
A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics|XPHB}) check against your spell save DC, breaking the bone spike and freeing itself on a success.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage (both initial and ongoing) increases by {@dice 1d10} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Spectral Fury
entries: You send forth three spectral duplicates of yourself to strike down enemies within 30 feet of you. You can order them to strike one target or several. Make a melee spell attack for each spectral duplicate. On a hit, a target takes {@damage 4d8} damage of your weapon's damage type.

You can then take a {@variantrule Bonus Action|XPHB} to move up to 30 feet in a straight line towards one of the targets without provoking {@variantrule Opportunity Attack|XPHB|Opportunity Attacks}, streaking through a spectral trail, and make a single melee weapon attack.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage of your spectral duplicate increases by {@dice 2d8} for each spell slot level above 3.

spell.name: Dread Scarecrow

m.text: a flute made of a femur worth 50+ GP

entries: You magically create the horrifying illusion of all your bones breaking and your body bending in impossible ways, accompanied by the sound of a shattered skull. Each creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius {@variantrule Sphere [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Sphere} centered on you must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or have the {@condition Frightened|XPHB} condition for the duration. While {@condition Frightened|XPHB} by this spell, a creature's {@variantrule Speed|XPHB} becomes 0 and it has the {@condition Prone|XPHB} condition, its legs giving out under fear. If an affected creature takes damage, it can repeat the saving throw at the end of its next turn, ending the effect on itself on a success.

spell.name: Maiden of Bones
entries: A creature within range must succeed on a Strength saving throw or be trapped inside an iron maiden formed of bone that appears in its space. The creature has the {@condition Restrained|XPHB} and {@condition Incapacitated|XPHB} conditions, is behind {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Total Cover}, can't be damaged by attacks or effects originating from outside, and takes {@damage 3d6} Piercing damage at the start of each of its turns as spikes of bone pierce its body.
At the end of each of its turns, a trapped creature can repeat the saving throw, escaping and ending the spell on a success.

The bone maiden has AC equal to 10 plus your spellcasting modifier, 80 {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB}, {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB} to Psychic and Poison damage, and {@variantrule Vulnerability|XPHB} to Bludgeoning damage. If the maiden is destroyed, the creature trapped inside is freed and the spell ends.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} and the maiden's {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} increase by 20 for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Marrow Transplant

m.text: a piece of spinal bone and a diamond worth 300+ GP, which the spell consumes

entries: You drain the bone marrow of a creature, attempting to steal its life force and transfer it to another creature of your choice. Make a ranged spell attack against a creature within range. On a hit, the target takes {@damage 4d6} Necrotic damage. Choose another creature within range; it regains a number of {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the damage dealt, or if it was dead for less than 1 minute, the creature returns to life with {@variantrule Hit Points|XPHB} equal to the number regained. If any of the targets do not have bones, the spell fails. This spell can't return to life a creature that has died of old age, nor can it restore any missing body parts.

entriesHigherLevel.name: Using a Higher-Level Spell Slot
entries: The damage increases by {@dice 1d6} for each spell slot level above 4.

spell.name: Forest of Dread
entries: You touch the ground beneath you and tree-like bones sprout from the ground in a 30-foot-radius, 20-foot-high {@variantrule Cylinder [Area of Effect]|XPHB|Cylinder} centered on you. Each creature of your choice in that area must make a Dexterity saving throw, taking {@damage 4d8} Piercing damage on a failed save, or half as much damage on a successful one.

For the duration, the area becomes {@variantrule Difficult Terrain|XPHB}, and when a creature moves into or within the area, it takes {@damage 2d8} Piercing damage for every 5 feet it travels; you are {@variantrule Immunity|XPHB|Immune} to this effect. The forest of dread provides {@variantrule Cover|XPHB|Half Cover} to any creatures inside the area. The bones disintegrate when the spell ends.

data.name: Lore Primer
entries: Luyarnha began five centuries ago as a fragile settlement born from an unprecedented alliance between humans and elves, forged after years of inconclusive warfare over the land. What started as a pragmatic compromise soon flourished: elven wisdom and longevity complemented human ambition, strength, and numbers, allowing the young city to prosper. Positioned between powerful realms and at the crossroads of major trade routes, it negotiated full sovereignty under a half-elven Silverblood regent and grew rapidly into a wealthy and influential kingdom. Protected by its neighbors and fortified against dangers from the wild southern frontier, the city enjoyed decades of prosperity as commerce expanded and its diverse population continued to grow.

Yet the very diversity that had fueled Luyarnha's rise eventually bred division. Cultural and religious conflicts fractured society and paralyzed the justice system, prompting the rise of Reinholdt "the Yellow" Silverblood, later known as the Godless King. Determined to impose unity, he centralized power, outlawed all religions, and replaced faith with state indoctrination and loyalty to the crown. His increasingly brutal rule crushed dissent and militarized the kingdom in pursuit of expansion. When he declared his intent to conquer the weakened elven realm, resentment ignited a revolution led largely by the Radiant Church and disillusioned citizens. The resulting civil war devastated the city until the king was betrayed and assassinated by his own brother, ending his tyrannical reign but leaving Luyarnha in chaos.

Those who were present during the Godless King's murder heard him talk in an impossible language, laying a curse upon Luyarnha with his last breath. No one knows what this posthumous act of spite entailed, though some speculate that he aimed to bring ruin upon the city he once ruled, to scourge the people who betrayed him. In the aftermath, the Church assumed temporary control while the surviving Silverblood lineage remained under watch, tasked with helping rebuild a fractured nation.

entries.name: Beginnings
entries: In lieu of the Godless King's fall, news of Luyarnha's vulnerability reached the monstrous nations of the south, who saw it as the opportune moment to strike. Under the sky of a crimson moon, the First War dawned on the city-state.

When the bells of war began to toll, emissaries were sent to the neighboring countries requesting help, in vain. The once-mighty human empire had already been reduced to ash, and the Elven Enclave struggled under the weight of its own internal strife, unable to spare either thought or soldier for the conflict brewing to their east.

Luyarnha was to stand alone. Yet, amidst these dire odds, the southern wall of the city, built years prior to protect against the seasonal bestial incursions, was now the core of its defense and survival, holding strong against the southern marauders. Though a handful of the vile beasts breached this bulwark, most of the war's remained outside the city's edges.

It was a dance of death and despair. Still, Luyarnha held firm, its fortified position allowing it to resist with a resilience that surprised even its own people. Aid also arrived from unexpected quarters. The cursed-bloods and the dwarves answered the call when the drums of war began to sound. The cursed-bloods, long treated as outcasts, proved invaluable. Their mastery of stonework bordered on the divine, and their tireless labor kept the walls standing against the relentless assault. Without them, Luyarnha would have fallen within months, a fact most tend to forget.

Thus, in the face of mounting odds, Luyarnha was able to weather the early stages of the First War, owing to the fortitude of its inhabitants and the unsung heroes who lent their hands to the city's survival.

entries.name: Guerilla Tactics
entries: The wheel of war churned mercilessly, and the scene in Luyarnha took a turn for the worse. The enemy changed its tactics. Guerrilla forces cloaked in illusion slipped through the chaos created by their rampaging beasts and infiltrated the city itself. Hidden among the populace, they lived as ordinary citizens until the moment came to strike. The southerners, wolves in sheep's clothing, bared their fangs only once within the heart of the city, spreading terror and bloodshed in equal measure. And so, Luyarnha found itself ensnared in a conflict of two fronts: one beyond its sturdy walls, the other festering within its very heart.

The city-state, overwhelmed by this maelstrom of violence and betrayal, strained under the burden. Holding the monstrous armies at bay outside the walls was burden enough. Hunting an unseen enemy moving quietly among the people proved a far more daunting task. Such was the cunning of the southern forces.

Before this reality, the Radiant Church unshackled the Obitus Scholare—a specialized task force born amidst the civil war—from all moral and legal restraint. Once formed to counter the arcane might of the royalty during the civil war, they were now assigned the task of forging human weapons that could turn the tide of war. As the conflict intensified, the Obitus were granted access to every artifact and fragment of arcane knowledge once guarded by the fallen royal house. Alongside them rose another body of scholars born from the city's desperation, the {@area Scions|00e|x}. Both factions, standing to gain from the war's grim bounty, crafted tools of destruction that might allow Luyarnha to retaliate.

The war continued its rampage, a juggernaut that trampled and erased the villages encircling Luyarnha, leaving nothing but trails of ruin in its wake. One such settlement was cruelly drowned in a flood of corrosive acid—a despicable act of cruelty by the southern invaders.

Meanwhile the war continued its brutal march. The countryside surrounding Luyarnha was ravaged, villages crushed beneath the advance of the southern armies. One settlement was annihilated when the invaders drowned it beneath a flood of corrosive acid. The battlefield was awash with death and despair, and the city's defenders began to falter. The walls still stood, but hope itself seemed close to collapse.
Then, at the bleakest hour, the Obitus Scholare announced a breakthrough.

entries.name: Shifting The Tide
entries: The Obitus unveiled their magnum opus, the first jaeger: an augmented warrior gifted with superhuman capabilities and tracking prowess. This warrior could not only root out the infiltrators within the city, but also slay the beasts that accompanied them, quickly neutralizing the threat festering inside Luyarnha's walls.

The first of these jaegers was Steinhardt, the bastard son of the Godless King. He, who was raised an orphan, stepped forth from the shadows to become a beacon of hope. Following Steinhardt's rise, a new breed of jaegers, trained by the Obitus and the Church, began to turn the tide against the invaders. To this day, jaegers born of the First War are christened the First Jaegers, and to this day no one but the Obitus knows the secret behind their creation—warriors born of the blood, made men by the blood, and undone by the blood.

Parallel to this, the Scions had their moment under the limelight. They birthed a wonder of artificial life: the {@race Manikin|SGEHPP}. These constructs, wrought from steel and lightning yet possessed of sentience, gave Luyarnha much-needed reinforcements and added a layer of defense against the encroaching southern tide.

These technological leaps turned the tide of war. The southerners' guerrilla tactics lost their edge, and the city's walls, which they had once come so close to breaching, now stood as an unyielding barrier. Thanks to the infrastructure established during the reign of the Godless King, Luyarnha could sustain itself even with its trade routes severed. In fact, it was the southerners who now faced the toll of prolonged war.
After years of bitter struggle, with famine threatening their ranks, the southern armies finally sounded their retreat. Luyarnha had won.

Yet in the wake of this conflict, there was no glory to bask in, no joy to revel in. The land had become a graveyard of fallen soldiers and shattered hopes, and what remained was a fragile peace few dared trust.

entries.name: The Radiant City
entries: The Radiant Church found itself shepherding a city groaning under the weight of exhaustion. Could it be that after seasons of oppression and conflict, the long-desired peace was within reach?

entries.name: Rebuilding Luyarnha
entries: In the decades succeeding the war, the once vibrant city of Luyarnha grew quiet, nursing its wounds after the savagery of both the civil war and the First War. Few held the heart to chase the southern nation back into the forests from which they sprang.

The citizens, having found solace in the Church's dedication and faith, resolved to entrust them with the reins of power, at least for the time being, amidst the political void left by the Silverblood royalty's downfall.

Yet the royal line did not vanish entirely, and a new queen ascended the throne. Though all the political power was in the hands of the Church, the Silverbloods retained a foothold in the power structure through the deal struck at the height of the civil war, strengthened further by Steinhardt's sweeping popularity. The Radiant Church recognized the value of the royal family's experience in war and statecraft and granted them a modest share of influence, albeit begrudgingly.

The once grand Spired District, now a ruin, was resurrected from its ashes and rechristened as the {@area New Bridge District|01f|x}. The Scions, tasked with orchestrating the mammoth repair efforts, deemed it an ideal location for their operations. Pouring vast resources into the restoration, they harnessed the abilities of their {@race Manikin|SGEHPP} creations to expedite the process.

The Obitus Scholare relocated to the confines of the {@area Grand Cathedral District|01a|x}, sharing its hallowed grounds with the Church's governing institutions. Here, they were entrusted with significant funds to further research initiatives intended to uplift the populace, a vision the Radiant Church eagerly fostered.

With political power secured, the Church found fertile ground for the spread of its teachings. Its faith reached far beyond Luyarnha's walls, carried along trade routes that now stretched to distant lands outside the old spheres of human and elven influence. Commerce returned with vigor, and with it came new technologies. Railways began to appear, binding regions together that had once seemed impossibly far apart.

Prosperity followed. Merchants, travelers, and fortune seekers flocked to the Radiant city, and vast wealth began to circulate through its markets. Yet memories of past invasions remained vivid. The city's great wall was reinforced with layers of stone and steel.

Conversely, this age of progress marked the slow decline of the arcane. Magic had always been rare, but the rise of technology placed power in the hands of ordinary people in ways the arcane never could. Nor did it carry the same harrowing aftermath, as the fate of osteomancy would soon make clear. During the catastrophe later called the Great Unchaining, that cursed art turned upon its own practitioners, unleashing horrors that claimed the lives of many scholars. In the end, the Church was forced to declare martial law to hunt down the monstrous remnants of the disaster and bring the nightmare to an end.

entries.name: Spreading Corruption
entries: Yet not all was blessed under the divine light. Whispers of grotesque beasts prowling the city's cobbled paths started stirring the air, hushed by the voices and fearful gazes of citizens dreading the return of the southern armies. However, these creatures seemed to be phantoms of the night, leaving no evidence of their existence in the morning light.

At first, the Church and its delegates staunchly dismissed such monstrous sightings, successfully easing the citizens' simmering panic. But as time passed, tales of nocturnal horrors multiplied. With each new day, the ghastly evidence mounted: a lifeless body discovered at dawn, trails of crimson on cobblestones, neighbors who vanished into the night and were never seen again.

As the public outcry grew, the Church's initial denial took on a stricter tenor. No longer were citizens allowed to venture out at nightfall as the threat began to reveal its terrifying reality. Instead, the Church dispatched its trained hunters into the darkness to combat these unseen beasts, while ordinary citizens were forced to seek refuge behind locked doors.

This wave of horrors appeared to originate from the {@area Ruby District|017|x}, the focal point of the Church's interventions. Yet, despite their warriors' valiant efforts, fresh monstrosities seemed to emerge each night. At last the Church acknowledged the danger openly and gave the growing calamity a name: the Scourge. Citizens willing to fight were called upon to defend their homes and their city.

The sealing of the Ruby District followed a Blood Moon—the 33rd of its kind. The Church calls these nights Hunts. The name is a deliberate act of propaganda: it places the focus around the hunters who stand ready, not the horrors that emerge from the crimson light. That night the creatures were driven into a vicious frenzy, and countless hunters were lost. The Ruby District, long teetering on the brink, was swallowed by the disaster.

Containment failed soon after. The Scourge began to seep into other districts of the city. At the same time, neighboring nations watched with rising alarm. They warned that if the plague within Luyarnha was not brought under control, they would unite to destroy the city themselves. The leaders of Luyarnha still remembered the strain of fighting on several fronts during the First War. Faced with that memory, they yielded to the pressure. The city was placed under total lockdown.

But the containment efforts fell short as the Scourge began to seep into other parts of the city. At the same time, growing pressure from neighboring nations forced the Church's hand. These powers warned that if the Scourge was not contained, they would unite to erase Luyarnha from existence. The leaders of Luyarnha still remembered the strain of fighting on several fronts during the First War and knew such a conflict would mean the end of their city. They yielded to the pressure. Luyarnha was placed under total lockdown.

entries.name: The Beginning of the End
entries: Since the arrival of the Scourge, the city of Luyarnha has been thrust into a pitiless struggle for existence. The scholars among them discerned the correlation between the city's fate and the whims of the moon, its cryptic shifts spelling doom for those caught in its pallid light. Once, these celestial oscillations were a secret known only to the intellectuals, a knowledge invaluable for predicting the ominous rise of the Blood Moons. Yet in recent times, the entire city has become privy to this terrifying spectacle, the silent dread of the cosmos etched on every face that dares look up at the inky sky.

Citizens voluntarily remain confined to their abodes, ceding the night to the hunters, their only protectors against the vile creatures birthed from the Scourge. Fear has become a constant companion in Luyarnha.

In this ceaseless battle, the city has endured thirty-four Hunts. Each one has ushered in a tide of terror and bloodshed, threatening the existence of thousands. Despite the overwhelming odds, the courageous hunters continue their relentless crusade.

However, Luyarnha has begun to realize a terrible truth—the Scourge is not waning. Instead, it is gaining momentum, escalating in its intensity and ferocity. Countless hours of desperate research have failed to yield a cure, as the affliction claims evermore victims. Fear courses through the halls of knowledge, as scholars begin to suspect that their hubris led them beyond the boundaries of mortal comprehension.

entries.name: Today
entries: Today Luyarnha is a gothic cage where the Radiant One's golden glow struggles to pierce a suffocating shroud of dread. The city-state continues its desperate, losing struggle against the Scourge—a bestial plague that turns neighbors into monsters—compounded by a brewing unrest between the domineering Radiant Church, the ambitious Scions, and the various marginalized factions who yearn to watch the immaculate towers of the elite burn.

Once a beacon of prosperity, the Radiant City has devolved in a race towards annihilation: from the opulent, rot-filled estates of the Sanctified District to the walled-off, blood-soaked slaughterhouse of the Ruby District. Survival über alles has become the motto of those who patrol moonlit streets slick with beast-blood, while the air hums with the volatile crackle of Scionic lightning and the heavy scent of incense.

entries.name: Beliefs
entries: The Radiant Faith began with the divine revelations of the Prophet Luminara, who foretold the coming Radiant Ascendancy—an era when the Radiant One's light would guide the world. What started as a quiet belief among a few devoted followers eventually spread across Luyarnha, centered on the worship of the nameless Radiant One, a deity known by many titles who grants blessings to the faithful, sometimes marked by golden pupils.

The Church teaches that true goodness is born from strength rather than weakness, urging its followers to face adversity with courage while also holding hope for a brighter future. They believe that there is a duality of light and darkness within every soul, where one's deeds determine whether they move toward heavenly ascension or damnation.

The faith rose to prominence during a time when religion was outlawed under the Godless King, whose brutal execution of Luminara transformed the prophet into a martyr and ignited a spiritual revival. Visions of the prophet after his death inspired followers and fueled the rapid expansion of the Church, whose acts of charity and miracles won the loyalty of the common people. This growing influence eventually sparked a civil conflict that ended with the fall of the Godless King and the Radiant Church assuming complete control of Luyarnha, guiding it into an age of prosperity that later became strained by internal corruption, and the ever-present threat of the Scourge.

entries.name: Church Powers
entries: The Radiant Church governs Luyarnha through three primary pillars, each led by a High-Apostle: the Radiant Order, the Obitus Scholare, and the Divine Enclave.

The Radiant Order serves as the Church's right hand and military backbone, managing the Militia of hunters and the Blood Cross healers who distribute the sacred Holy Tonic. Within the order, the Grey Templars, a force known only to a select few, act as elite defenders against evils far beyond the Scourge. High-Apostle Logarius directs these so-called grey-knights with an unyielding hand, focusing on the preservation of hope and the common goal of safeguarding the city's families.

As the Church's voice, the Obitus Scholare initially forged tools for defense but has since descended into sacrilege and inhuman experimentation. They operate under the cold philosophy that mortals can only be saved through ascension, justifying macabre trials that include harvesting Great Ones' fluids and etching runes into human skulls. Although they successfully created the Jaegers, their pursuit of cosmic knowledge became so erratic that they eventually relocated their most forbidden research to the clandestine Cosmic Seminary. Their thirst for power is so insatiable that some suspect the {@area Obitus Scholare|00b|x} may have birthed the Scourge during a failed attempt to beckon the moon.

The Divine Enclave acts as the left hand of the Radiant One, managing information, morale, and justice through its three branches. The Luminary Scribes serve as investigators and censors who safeguard the Grand Library, often hiding sensitive truths that conflict with Church doctrine. Alongside them, the Ministry of Light rekindles hope through public sermons and provides the essential incense and weapon blessings that keep the beasts at bay. Judicial matters are settled by the House of Blood, an institution that utilizes torture combined with {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB} spells to ensure that only the absolute truth surfaces during trials. This brutal justice is applied to both accusers and defenders, to settle matters swiftly, and discourage false declarations.

entries.name: The Scions
entries: Birthed amidst the civil war, from an audacious ambition to challenge the divine through science, this secular faction of "wannabe gods" regards the Radiant Church's rituals as little more than futile theatrics. This hostility towards the powers that be is made possible by the city's absolute reliance on Scionic technology. Their headquarters, the Scions' Fortress, looms as a gothic monolith over the {@area New Bridge District|01f|x}, its stone façade bristling with a multitude of lightning rods that pierce the sky like the spines of an ancient beast. Within these electrified walls, the whirr of complex machinery and the hum of high-voltage generators fuel a relentless industrial engine, producing everything from life-sustaining electricity to the lethal Galespire Coils used for maritime defense.

At the fortress's summit lies the macabre Resurrection Chamber, a mechanized cathedral of conductive cables and metallic appendages where skeletal structures are grotesquely appended with machinery and animated by the raw force of thunderstorms. These cadaverous subjects are sourced from the Bone Vault, an underground repository stocked with remains plundered from communal graveyards and ancient prehistoric bones harvested from royal catacombs. Reanimated entities that survive this volatile process are stored within holding pens of graphite and glass, where they are scrutinized and subjugated into mindless servants, hidden away from the prying eyes of the Church.

The Scions' crowning achievement is the {@race Manikin|SGEHPP}, an entity of ivory and gold gifted life through electricity to serve as a tireless, expendable soldier. While these machines were intentionally designed with limited intellectual growth to ensure obedience, a disastrous attempt to bestow full sentience resulted in the revolt of Malach, the angel of flesh, who slaughtered dozens of Scions before vanishing into the Shrouded District. Today, the fortress's construct workshops stand mostly silent due to scarcity of materials caused by the city's lockdown, leaving the Scions to brood over their dwindling numbers while guarding their library of trade secrets with lethal force

entries.name: The Forsaken
entries: Born from the bitter dregs of abandonment and rejection, The Forsaken are a violent alliance of {@race Scourgeborne|SGEHPP} and marginalized races who have forged a self-sustaining society within the {@area Ruby District|017|x}. They dream of an independent district liberated from the overbearing yoke of the Radiant Church. Their leader, a formidable half-orc nursing resentment toward the ruling class, wields the devastating Earthbreaker powers. He single-handedly challenged the district's barricades to liberate his surrogate family, though his attempt left him severely wounded. The Forsaken lack a concrete alternative to the current governance, instead focusing on destructive rhetoric and rigorous training, an effort which has begun to seep into the city's cracks, drawing in those exhausted by the current rule. They currently seek secret knowledge related to gravity and the jaegers, in hope of turning the tide of their struggle.

entries.name: Malach's Angels
entries: A clandestine insurrection of sentient manikins known as Malach's Angels is rising within the Shrouded District. Led by the uncompromising Malach, these living automata seek to end the age of flesh, replacing it with the certainty of steel. The movement has reached a terrifying turning point with the abduction of a high-ranking Scion, whose expertise has allowed the rebels to establish a hidden factory for limitless "reproduction". Now, driven by an insatiable hunger for vengeance, the Angels launch violent raids against the Scions to plunder the raw materials necessary to swell their mechanical ranks, setting the stage for an uprising that threatens to eradicate all organic life in Luyarnha.

entries.name: Abyss Watchers
entries: Birthed within the suffocating soot of the Shrouded District, the cult of the Abyss Watcher offers sanctuary to the faithfuls who have been abandoned by the light of the Radiant One. Their deity is said to feast upon the very gods the Radiant Church protects, though its true agenda remains unknown. Only its most unhinged followers claim to be privy to the deity's actual motives. Devotees of the Abyss gather in hidden sanctuaries to perform arcane rituals that grant them the unsettling ability to nourish their god by consuming the flesh of both man and beast—an act that blesses them with preternatural strength. But such carnal devotion comes with a heavy price as the act of consumption triggers a maelstrom of turbulent passions that can drive a believer toward reckless impulses. Through great cunning, they have managed to echo the rituals of those who swear the {@subclass Eldritch Hunt|Paladin|XPHB|SGEHPP|Oath of the Eldritch Hunt}, these cultists have even managed to inconspicuously infiltrate the ranks of the grey-knights.

entries.name: The Sanctified District
entries: The Sanctified District is the exemplification of Luyarnha's enlightenment, where opulent spires and lush, Eden-like gardens mask a core curdling with corruption. Here, the rising Moongold family amasses wealth in the form of celestial alloys and Church favor, and greedy aristocrats shake the city's economic foundations under the weight of their "legal" counterfeiting. Behind the masks of decadent masquerades and the blood-soaked entertainment of the Grand Colosseum, a hidden threat looms: nobles vanish only to be replaced by eerily lifelike wax statues, children are haunted by spectral lullabies, and an insatiable, beast-like thirst begins to claim those who indulge too deeply in the district's noxious luxuries.

entries.name: Silverblood Castle
entries: Dominating the district from its high-ground perch, the Silverblood Castle is a gothic fortress of jagged spires and brooding parapets that physically manifests the divide between the privileged elite and the wretched masses. It is a house built on fratricide and fragile pacts, currently ruled by Queen Victoria Silverblood, who must navigate the treacherous waters of a resentful Church, a cursed lineage, and the ambitious machinations of her own kin. Deep beneath its stone foundations lie macabre catacombs filled with eldritch remains and the restless corpses of the first osteomancers, serving as both a royal burial site for the "Godless King" and a secret training ground for the Shadows, the crown's elusive cadre of assassins. Within its walls, secrets are guarded as fiercely as the throne itself—from a princess hidden in a chamber of unalloyed gold to a forbidden portal that leads to a Nightmare Realm.

entries.name: The Waterfront District
entries: Once the pulsing artery of Luyarnha's global trade, the Waterfront District has succumbed to a chilling, desolate silence under the weight of the city's quarantine. The resplendent bronze of the Gilded Harbor now sits tarnished, its opulent quays abandoned save for a few desperate fisheries and dive bars where patrons whisper of otherworldly influences mutating the populace into grotesque aberrations. While the river provides a natural barricade against the land-bound Scourge, causing local property values to surge, the district remains a labyrinth of shadows dominated by the enigmatic Victorian Masonia, a clandestine society of cursed-bloods who pull the city's political strings from the shadows. Between the industrious but dwindling Shipwright's Quarters and the mysterious disappearances of the city's sailors, the district is slowly morphing into a haunt of aquatic horrors.

entries.name: Bastille Key and the Abyssal Keep
entries: Floating on the Moryanne river that delimitates the district, Bastille Key is an island of stone and steel that has transformed from a vital maritime checkpoint into a sinister stronghold of the Y'ha-nthlei, mind-washed dwarves who have submerged a Radiant Cathedral to worship their dormant, abyssal deity. At the heart of this island lies the Abyssal Keep, a colossal penitentiary designed to contain the continent's most dangerous offenders through a ruthless hierarchy of incarceration. This inescapable fortress, the culmination of Luyarnha's brutal justice system, is patrolled by heartless mechanical constructs and harbors the wrongfully imprisoned Fire Dancers. While its Upper Grounds offer a semblance of humanity, the Silent Depths plunge the most dangerous inmates, oft spellcasters whose tongues and hands have been severed to prevent magic, into a realm of magical darkness and madness.

entries.name: The Ruby District
entries: Once the lush agricultural heart of Luyarnha, the Ruby District has been transformed into a ruined tapestry of decayed structures and scarlet maple trees, a haunting reflection of the blood spilt upon its cold stones. Nestled geographically beneath the rest of the city, it was abruptly isolated by military forces in a midnight lockdown intended to contain the eruption of the Scourge, a betrayal that culminated in the "Day of the Blood Ruby"—a horrific slaughter where heavy artillery met the desperate surge of residents attempting to flee their new prison. Now a lawless testing ground for freshly initiated jaegers and a hunting floor for those seeking lost relics of the First War, the district rots from within; its sewers teem with the eerie howls of beasts, while the Radiant Church prepares a "scorched earth" contingency to incinerate the entire sector. Amidst this desolation, the enigmatic Carmella labors within her greenhouse to cultivate miraculous cures from parasitic Cordyceps Sinensis, offering an implausible glint of hope even as the upper echelons plot to turn the district into a final, purifying inferno.

entries.name: The Shrouded District
entries: Cloaked in a perpetual twilight of suffocating smog and covered by the shadow of the Grand Cathedral, the Shrouded District serves as Luyarnha's industrial cellar and a haven for those seeking refuge from the Radiant One's light. Beneath its soot-stained surface, a resilient population of humans and dwarves toils within labyrinthine coal mines to power the city's steam heart, even as they succumb to lethal diseases, from lung fire to carnal rot. The district is a land of stark paradoxes: while the School of Eldritch Tongue conducts high-stakes translations of ancient Deep Speech in secret chambers, a flourishing narcotic trade fueled by the decadence of the upper-district aristocracy poisons the impoverished masses with psychoactive scraps. Between the flesh-consuming rituals dedicated to the false god that is the Abyss Watcher and the tar-drowned horrors that erupt from the depths of the mines, the district is a volatile landscape of poverty and despair.

entries.name: Paterna Iter
entries: The Paterna Iter District serves as a vital artery of Luyarnha, a grand ancestral road winding toward the Grand Cathedral, transformed from a hallowed pilgrim's path into the city's commercial and agricultural lifeline. While the ground level has devolved into a warzone littered with barricades, soldiers and makeshift hospitals, the district's denizens stay resilient. Led by elven magic and orcish labor, they have converted residential buildings into layered vertical farms that stave off famine. Yet, the miracles of their growth wanes, as the aqueduct supplying the district water rots from within. Above the chaos, the Jaeger's Workshop churns out the specialized steel necessary for survival, and the Grand Central Station, silenced by the Scourge, prepares to welcome a rogue train barreling toward the city walls, its contents unknown. Beneath the district lies a subterranean black market where esoteric knowledge, from Nightmare Realms to aristocratic gossip, is auctioned. Ever-shifting it avoids the prying eyes of the Radiant Church and roaming beasts alike.

entries.name: Grand Cathedral
entries: Standing at the city's heart, the{@b Grand Cathedral} is a gargantuan edifice that functions as its own town, covering five square kilometers with a central spire tall enough to scrape the heavens. Once a repository of Luyarnha's diverse faiths, it was purged of all but the worship of the Radiant One, transforming into an impregnable bastion for the city's elite warriors and high clergy. Inside, the Grand Nave hums with a continuous cycle of hymns that cease only at sundown, while outside, grand gardens mask formidable ramparts and the sickly sweet aroma of incense serves as a potent deterrent against the creatures of the Scourge.

High above, a trinity of chimes governs the city's survival; most notable among them, the Bell of Death rattles the soul with a trifold toll to signal the rise of the Blood Moon. Between these peaks sits the Luminary Repository, a vault of wisdom where even forbidden lore is meticulously organized.
The cathedral is spiritually and physically anchored by the Three Spires, each symbolizing one the Radiant Faith's core values:

entries.name: The Pillar of Fortitude (Strength)
entries: This spire functions as a grueling training ground for hunters, housing an urban labyrinth designed to forge warriors who can thrive amidst the chaos of the Scourge.

entries.name: The Pillar of Blood (Virtue)
entries: Its base contains the House of Blood, where the city's merciless judicial trials are held, while its summit houses a radiant chamber where the high-apostles convene to deliberate on the future of the city.

entries.name: The Pillar of Faith (Faith)
entries: This tower is home to an endless spiral staircase that resonates with the hymns of the congregation, ascending toward the Observatory, the crown of the spire where scholars attempt to decode the celestial whispers of the Great Ones.

Life within the residential quarters is a cycle of divine communion and mandatory service, as all young residents must endure a three-year conscription under the Radiant Order regardless of disability. Yet, this sanctity belies a darker history; the Asylum, once a political prison and experimental chamber for the Obitus Scholare, was the place of birth of the illustrious Jaegers. Though long disaffected, tormented wails continue to leak from its depths.

entries.name: New Bridge District
entries: Once known as the Spired District before the First War reduced it to dust, the New Bridge District has been reborn as a secular, brutalist bastion of resilience. It is bordered by the Steelsurge Bridge—a marvel of engineering spanning the Moryanne River—where azure lights illuminate a drawbridge that has sat open and motionless since the city's lockdown began. Financed by the Scions and built by the tireless labor of cursed-bloods, the district has become Luyarnha's primary hub for construction and carpentry, notably housing the city's only monument to the masked workers who garner the suspicion of many. Despite its industrious rhythm dictated by the Scion's headquarters, the area is haunted by deep scars: ruined pillars from the old city attract frenzied moon-worshippers, while a network of orphanages overflows from the lives shattered by the Scourge and the Hunts.

entries.name: Barbarian - Path of the Lightning Vessel

entries: "Even while her body was falling apart, she was still fighting. Even when her arm was being torn to shreds, she was still fighting. When all her allies fell, she stood and kept fighting. Only when the battle was won did she draw her last breath, but she was still standing. Not even death could break her."
